title: Authoring eval
summary: Can a model write a correct benchmark.json from a paper? Every model gets the same single prompt per case and answers with one JSON object, which is scored key by key against the curated spec. A JSON repair turn is on by default; running the solver, with its own repair loop, is opt-in. Both kinds of repair are reported apart from authoring accuracy.

groups.label: for each case
groups.detail: Runs once per case, before any model is called.

groups.label: solver attempts
groups.detail: Attempt 0 runs the authored JSON. Each failed attempt can trigger one repair call, up to --solver-feedback-turns.

nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.detail: One entry per case: extracted paper text, scope.md, and the curated benchmark.json that is the answer key. Built from benchmarks/ by --dataset, and automatically on the first run.

nodes.label: Model roster
nodes.detail: Model ids and per-model max_tokens, temperature, timeout. Models marked metered cost money and are refused without --allow-metered.

nodes.label: Guide + schema
nodes.detail: The authoring guide, the physics modules and the schema. The schema is sent with its prose descriptions stripped.

nodes.label: Solver preflight
nodes.detail: The THCM-FEM CLI exists and the OOFEM bindings import. Fails the run before any API call is made.

nodes.label: Solve curated JSON
nodes.detail: Runs the answer key through the same solver. It keeps its plots and reference curves (benchmarks/<case>/reference/ is copied in), so its plots are the picture to compare against. A failed baseline means the solver, not the model, is the problem for that case.

nodes.label: Build prompt
nodes.detail: prompts/author_benchmark.md filled with the guide, modules, schema, the case scope and the paper text (cut at --max-paper-chars). Identical for every model.

nodes.label: Author call
nodes.detail: One chat completion, no tools. JSON-repair and solver-repair turns continue this same conversation.

nodes.label: Parse JSON
nodes.detail: Outcome ok, truncated, unparseable, refused or error. The record keeps the FIRST reply's outcome, so the parse rate still measures the model even when a repair turn fixed it.

nodes.label: candidate.json
nodes.detail: The latest accepted object. Every solver-repair revision is also kept as candidate.attempt-N.json.

nodes.label: Compare to answer key
nodes.detail: Section-weighted, key-by-key comparison with the curated spec. physics, materials, boundary and initial conditions are strict; results.queries is matched loosely; plots and reference curves are not scored. Re-run after every accepted revision.

nodes.label: THCM-FEM run
nodes.detail: Execution projection first: the model's reference curves are removed, save_db is forced, VTU and checkpoints are off. Then thcm mesh and thcm oofem --on-nonconverged abort. Status ok means at least one query row was written; a plotting crash after that still counts as ok.

nodes.label: Results + plots
nodes.detail: Query rows as CSV, the model's own plots (reference curves removed), and the classified status with a log tail.

nodes.label: run.json
nodes.detail: Every call's outcome, scores, solver attempts and repairs. Rewritten after each call, so an interrupted sweep keeps its progress.

nodes.label: Leaderboard
nodes.detail: Models ranked by accuracy with per-section columns, the first-try parse rate, execution results, and a census of the mistakes several models share.

nodes.label: Analyst diagnosis
nodes.detail: One fixed analyst model gets the paper, the answer key, the candidate and its findings, and groups the findings by cause (model error, comparator artifact, ambiguous paper). Never changes a score.

edges.label: JSON repair
edges.when: the reply has content but no parseable JSON object (unparseable, or truncated with nothing recovered)
edges.carries: the parser error and ~200 characters either side of it with the position marked; a truncated reply is also asked to drop _comment prose

edges.label: answer key
edges.carries: the curated benchmark.json, which the model never sees

edges.label: solver repair
edges.when: status is not ok: mesh or solve failed, timeout, or no query rows
edges.carries: status, stage, message, row count, column names, a numeric summary and the last solver log lines, but never the answer key or the score findings

params.help: Which models to call. Default: the entries marked default in models.yaml.
Which dataset cases to run. Default: every case with a paper.
Stop after the first N selected cases.

Permit models that cost money. Without it, metered models are refused before any call.
The OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Default: endpoint in models.yaml.
Cut the paper text at this length before it goes into the prompt.
Relative tolerance under which two numbers count as equal.
How many times an unparseable reply gets its parser error back. 0 disables the loop.
Run each candidate through THCM-FEM after scoring.
How many repair calls a failed solver run may trigger.
Also run the curated answer key through the solver, once per case.
Which THCM-FEM backend runs the JSON.
Seconds allowed for each mesh and each solve.
Keep VTU field output (large; off by default).
Re-score an existing run's candidates. No API calls, no solver.
Run an existing run's candidates through the solver. No API calls, no repair turns.
Write the leaderboard for a run (default: the latest).
Ask one analyst model why each spec is wrong. The analyst is metered, so it also needs --allow-metered.
Rebuild dataset/ from benchmarks/.
Send each model a one-word request to see which ones answer, then exit.
List what the endpoint serves, split into free and metered, then exit.
One-line description, used by worker.sh to list the jobs.
Print where runs are written.
